stemMd: The primary purpose of the passage is to
instructionsMd: Answer on the basis of what is stated or implied in the passage.

options.label: A
options.textMd: explain why lithium-ion batteries have fallen in cost more rapidly than competing storage technologies

options.label: B
options.textMd: argue that a standard cost measure conceals a difference between two storage roles, one of which no current payment rewards

options.label: C
options.textMd: compare the round-trip efficiencies of the leading grid-scale storage technologies

options.label: D
options.textMd: describe the engineering obstacles that prevent underground hydrogen caverns from storing energy across seasons

options.label: E
options.textMd: recommend that utilities abandon lithium-ion batteries in favour of iron-air cells, pumped water and hydrogen caverns

explanationMd:
A primary-purpose question is answered by the shape of the whole passage, not by any one sentence.

Trace the structure. Paragraph 1 introduces the installed-cost metric and says the assumption behind it fails, because daily-cycling storage and seasonal storage earn their money in completely different ways. Paragraph 2 says this difference has produced two separate engineering agendas and that collapsing them into one number overstates the progress of the second. Paragraph 3 says tariffs pay for the first agenda and not the second, so the seasonal problem persists for commercial rather than technical reasons.

So the passage does two things: it exposes what a single cost measure hides, and it identifies the missing payment for the neglected role. Choice B states exactly that pair.

A reliable way to check a primary-purpose answer: ask whether the choice covers the last paragraph as well as the first. Only B does — the phrase "no current payment rewards" accounts for paragraph 3, which every other choice leaves out entirely.

distractorRationale.a: The passage mentions that lithium-ion installed costs have fallen, but it never explains why, and it uses the fact only as the premise it goes on to question. A supporting premise is being mistaken for the purpose.
distractorRationale.e: This overstates the passage. The author says lithium-ion "serves" the first agenda well and is merely "the wrong tool" for the second, which is a claim about matching technology to role, not a recommendation to abandon a technology.
distractorRationale.d: The passage explicitly denies this: the final sentence says the seasonal problem persists "not because the engineering is impossible, but because no one is paid to solve it." This choice reverses the author's conclusion.
distractorRationale.c: Efficiency appears in one clause of paragraph 2, where the author notes that the second agenda tolerates wasting half the energy. No efficiencies are compared, and a single detail cannot be the purpose of the whole passage.

accessibilityText: Question asking for the primary purpose of the accompanying three-paragraph passage about electricity grid storage. Five options describe different possible purposes.

independentSolve.workingNotes: The passage attacks the single installed-cost / 'levelised cost of storage' metric for collapsing two distinct storage roles, and closes with 'nothing pays an asset for the option value... no one is paid to solve it' - exactly B. A, D and E describe details the passage never develops, and C overstates: the passage says lithium-ion is the wrong tool only for the seasonal role, not that utilities should abandon it.
